title: The Stilling of the Forty Sails

arc.title: The Stilling of the Forty Sails
arc.villain: Maelgorn the Windless, a storm-priest who came ashore with the Long Gale and was buried beneath the headland for trying to cage the wind — and who is trying again, one sail at a time, through his hooded servants the Still Choir
arc.stakes: If the Still Choir empties the coast wind into Maelgorn's brass cages, Millhaven's forty sails stop, the mills grind nothing, the harbour goes glassy and no ship leaves it — a whole grain coast starving in fine weather. And a storm-priest with the wind in his fist has no reason to stop at one town.

acts.title: The Sails That Would Not Turn
acts.hook: Three of the outland mills among the barley have stopped dead — canvas whole, gears sound, and not a breath of air inside their yards though the hedges outside are thrashing. Cobb Trethaway has a ledger of carts that have not come down and a speech about roads he cannot stop giving, and he wants someone to walk out to Barrowdown Outmill and find out who chained its sails. He shares his pastry tin while he asks.
acts.adventure_theme: Barrowdown Outmill, a grain-mill deep in the barley seized by the hooded Still Choir, who nail iron wind-sigils to every beam
acts.tone_notes: Gold barley under a hard blue sky; the eerie hush of dead air inside a working wind; warm dusty mill-timber turning wrong.

acts.title: The Calm on Coalhaul Bay
acts.hook: The bay has gone flat as hammered tin for six days, the grain ships sit at anchor going nowhere, and a becalmed hulk has drifted in on the tide with its crew safe, bewildered, and all their canvas gone rigid with salt-frost. Odile Kerrick, shouting over weather that isn't there, has traced the dead air to the drowned chapel-light out on Gullstone Reef. She'll lend the rescue boat to anyone who can coil a rope properly.
acts.adventure_theme: The Gullstone Light, a half-drowned lighthouse-chapel on the reef where the Still Choir's chanters fill brass wind-cages at the tide-line
acts.tone_notes: Silver dead-calm water, weed-green stone, kelp bells; wondrous rather than grim — the sea holding its breath.

acts.title: What the Shrine Floor Warned About
acts.hook: Ammeline has finished the last two lines of the old cliff-tongue in her shrine floor, and they are a warning: something was buried further along the headland, and the ribbons of the town were meant to keep it sleeping. Now the ribbons hang slack and a cold draught comes up out of the turf. She asks the party plainly to go down before the Choir opens the last cage — and sends them first to the shrine bench, where Elder Thistlewaite remembers what came ashore with the Long Gale.
acts.adventure_theme: The Cairn of Forty Sails, a wind-vault buried beneath the headland, where Maelgorn the Windless waits at his brass weathervane engine
acts.tone_notes: Torchlight on ancient carved sails, air roaring in stone throats, then the great bright wind breaking free over the cliff at dawn.

quest.title: The Sails That Would Not Turn
quest.text: Three of Millhaven's outland mills have stopped dead in the middle of the barley — canvas whole, gears sound, and not a breath of air inside their yards though the hedgerows outside thrash like the sea. Alderman Cobb Trethaway has a ledger full of carts that never came down the road and no notion who could chain a wind. Walk out to Barrowdown Outmill and find who has hushed it. Tullow Bramblebrook gathers on those downs at dawn and can tell you which hedge-path to take.

materialization.arrival: The coast road bends around a shoulder of green and Millhaven is suddenly all of itself at once: whitewashed cottages in slate-blue tiers spilling down to a crescent harbour bright as hammered tin, and above them the windmills, sails turning in slow white unison against a hard blue sky. Flour dust lies pale on the cobbles and rises in little ghosts around your boots; gulls argue over the fish-quay, gears creak somewhere behind every wall, and the Mill Bell lets out one deep boom that you feel in your knees. A girl with a bread basket appraises your armour like a shopkeeper counting stock, a halfling voice from the great retired mill above promises somebody chowder in a tone that permits no refusal, and the wind off the bay pushes at your back as though hurrying you along. Inland, past the gold barley downs, three of the forty sails stand perfectly, unnaturally still.

root.speaker: npc
root.text: Ah — travellers, armed ones, and not a moment too soon. Cobb Trethaway, grain-factor and alderman, and I shall be brief, which I say as a courtesy rather than a promise. Have a pastry from the tin, there's a good soul, and let me show you a ledger that is missing eleven carts.

choices.label: What's wrong with the mills, Alderman?
We've been out there. It didn't go well.
We'll take the pastry and think on it.

carts.speaker: npc
carts.text: Not robbed — nobody's hurt, thank the Wind, they simply never came down. Barrowdown, Hollowsail, and the Nine Furlong outmill: three of my finest and not a bushel of meal out of any of them this fortnight. A town runs on flour the way a cart runs on wheels, and I will not preside over a Millhaven that has to buy its own bread from the Saltmarch.

mills.speaker: npc
mills.text: That is the part I cannot put in a ledger. Canvas whole, gears greased, nothing broken — and no air inside the yard. You stand at the gate with the hedge thrashing at your shoulder and step through and it is dead calm as a cellar. Farmhand who reported it said the sails looked ashamed.

choices.label: Who'd be out there to do it?
We'd want to ask around town first.

hooded.speaker: npc
hooded.text: Hooded folk in grey, is what the reapers say, going quiet through the barley and singing something with no tune in it. I have written to the wardens twice. The wardens are three days' ride and my carts are today.

choices.label: Three days isn't so long. We'll consider it.

accept.speaker: npc
accept.text: Splendid — splendid, and I shall keep my speech about the western roads for the harvest supper, which is the greatest gift I have to give. Take the hedge-path, not the cart track, and speak first to Tullow Bramblebrook at the Green Door; he walks those downs before the sun does and knows every stile by name. Pastries for the road. Insist.

returned.speaker: npc
returned.text: Wind and weather — sit down, sit down, you're bleeding on my scales. No, I'll hear no apology; I sent you into a thing nobody in this town understands and you came back, which is eleven carts better than my drivers managed. Bessa will feed you and Mother Havelock will scold you, in that order, and then — if you've the heart for it — the mill is still standing still.

choices.label: We'll go back. Properly, this time.
Give us a day to mend first.

root.speaker: npc
root.text: Oh — hello. Mind the door, there's marsh-mallow drying. That's for coughs, mostly, though Mother says... sorry. You'll be the ones Cobb's been telling. About the mills.

choices.label: You walk those downs. What have you seen?
We'll let you get back to your drying.

seen.speaker: npc
seen.text: The hedgerow birds have gone. Not flown south — gone sideways, down to the cliffs, all of them, and the hares with them. Things go out of a place before people notice the place has changed. There's grey folk in the barley too. They don't tread a path. That's the bit I don't like.

nopath.speaker: npc
nopath.text: Nine miles of hedge and I know every gap a boot's made in forty years. There's no new gap. They came out of the ground or they came out of the air, and neither of those is a thing I want to say out loud in Mother's kitchen.

path.speaker: npc
path.text: Take the stile behind the Mealmarket, follow the blackthorn to the leaning stone, then keep the wind on your left cheek all the way. When you can't feel it any more — that's the yard. You'll have stepped inside before you know you have.

choices.label: Keep the wind on our left. Good luck to us.
Anything growing out there worth carrying?

herbs.speaker: npc
herbs.text: Yellow tansy by the stile, and there's a good hedge-thyme past the leaning stone — chew it if your head goes light. Bring me a sprig if there's any left standing. Barley's tall this year. It shouldn't be so quiet in it.

root.speaker: npc
root.text: Sit — sit, no, that chair, the other one wobbles and I'll not have you spilling good chowder on the boards. Names after, bowls first, that's the house rule and I made it, so it's a good one. Bessa Cobblewick, and you've the look of folk who've walked further than they've eaten.

choices.label: What's the talk in here about the still mills?

room.speaker: npc
room.text: Beds in the round, up the spiral, and the sails turn over you all night which folk either love or complain about exactly once. Boots off, and I'll leave bread by the door for the morning. Sleep like the dead and wake up better than them.

talk.speaker: npc
talk.text: Barley folk come down and say their yards have gone quiet, and I say eat, and they eat, and then they say it again slower. Truth is I've three rooms kept for three drivers who've not come down that road yet. I'll not let them out. They're paid up in my book whether they know it or not.

going.speaker: npc
going.text: Then you'll go fed, and that's not a kindness, that's a condition. And you'll come back down — I'll keep a room, and don't you dare make me keep it long. Perrin will want your whole story and you may lie to him about the size of things, everyone does.

choices.label: We'll be back for the chowder.

chowder.speaker: npc
chowder.text: That's the sensible answer. No sea-fennel in it, before you ask — that was last month and we have all agreed to forget it. Forty years of my mother's recipes under this bar and I still can't leave well enough alone.

choices.label: It's the best on the coast, Bessa.
And a room, while we're being sensible.

flavor.nib_sowerby: You want the Alderman? Weighing-scales, blue coat, talking — he's always talking. A copper to guide you, or free if you'll tell me what a wyvern smells like.
flavor.grendorn_haleblack: HOLD IT UP. No — up, to the light. Aye, that grip'll cost you a thumb by midsummer, and I'll not sell you steel till you tell me plain what you mean to cut with it.
flavor.priestess_ammeline_roke: Tie a ribbon on the rail before you go inland — no, I don't know that it works. I know that people who tie them come back and tell me about it, which is close enough for a working craft.
flavor.perrin_ashlow: You're adventurers! Is that a real notch or a decoration, how far can you walk in a day, do you want your horses brushed — I'm the fastest legs in Millhaven, ask anyone, ask Bessa.
